exceptions.rationale: Legacy SQLite orchestration combines discovery, routing, CRUD, import/export, change overlays, and SQL console responsibilities; v2.5.0 adds OPFS auto-discovery, the Rust-backed snapshot cache/dirty-check, and automatic change tracking on top of the existing SIZE-01 debt. Bumped mechanically to unblock release — the owed split (snapshot/diff/discovery orchestration into their own composables) is tracked, not resolved, by this entry.

Legacy ADB command adapter still combines device, package, file, shell, reverse, and parsing capabilities; keep stable while capability command modules are extracted. Bumped from 1950 for classify_am_start_output() (v2.0.0) — a small, well-tested fix for a real false-positive bug, not scope growth; extracting one helper out of the cohesive app-launch flow would be an arbitrary split, not a real module boundary. Bumped from 2000 for emulator device listing (v2.2.0) — the AVD-aware branch of device enumeration belongs with the adb device parsing it extends; the emulator's own launch/discovery logic already lives in the separate commands/emulator.rs module. Bumped from 2009 to 2045 for async IPC (UI rewrite R0.1) — every command now hands its blocking body to run_blocking so ADB I/O never runs on the main thread; the per-command wrappers stay beside the commands they guard. The split into capability modules is scheduled with the R7 device rebuild.

Mirror backend combines stream lifecycle, codecs, capture, input, and event adapters; v2.4.0 adds bundled scrcpy binary resolution across release platforms, while MIR-01 owns the staged runtime split. Bumped from 1284 to 1379 for scrcpy 4.x protocol support (v2.4.3) — the server shifted its video-header layout (a new session packet, renumbered CONFIG/KEY_FRAME flag bits) and this fix adds version-aware parsing for both the handshake and per-frame path; splitting the added branches out would fragment one wire-format concern across files, not draw a real module boundary. Bumped from 1379 to 1401 for async IPC (UI rewrite R0.1) — screenshot, screen-size, keyevent and scrcpy launch/stop now run off the main thread through run_blocking; MIR-01 still owns the runtime split.
IndexedDB table combines TanStack configuration, editing actions, change overlays, virtualization, and presentation; approved pending responsibility extraction.
Replay database surface coordinates IndexedDB and SQLite snapshots, changes, filters, dialogs, and tables; REC-01 owns further capability separation.
IndexedDB explorer remains an orchestration surface for routing, metadata, paging, mutations, imports, exports, changes, and dialogs; approved pending focused composables.

SQLite backend currently combines discovery, queries, writes, metadata, export, and file synchronization adapters; v2.5.0 adds the cheap native dirty-check stat used by automatic change tracking. Bumped mechanically to unblock release, approved pending service-oriented command extraction.
Recording database adapter owns snapshot persistence, paging, schema conversion, and replay queries; REC-01 will split persistence from command adaptation.
Interactive documentation preview combines device, inspector, storage, console, and settings demonstrations; approved pending extraction into capability preview components.

Durable task runtime accumulated task/run lifecycle, the append-only event log, reasoning ownership and handoff, trace paging, promotion, cancellation and the MCP-facing surface across CB-77 to CB-83. CB-90 cut it from 1589 to 1199 lines by extracting every seam that could move without changing behaviour: runRegistryTypes.ts (the shared interfaces, extracted first to break a cycle between the registry and its helpers), runRegistryHelpers.ts (the module-level functions that already took explicit parameters) and runRegistryRuntimeState.ts (createRuntimeState, a pure builder). All 585 tests pass with no assertion edited and no importer changed. What remains is the returned object literal whose methods call each other through `this` (cancelTask -> this.cancelRun, resumeTask -> this.startGoal); moving those changes `this` binding, which is a behaviour change CB-90 explicitly forbids. Extracting the remaining enqueuePersistence closures would reach roughly 1000 lines and still exceed the threshold, so it was rejected as a half-measure. The owed work — converting the this-coupled methods into free functions over an explicit registry context — is tracked, not resolved, by this entry. The file grew 61 lines during the CB-90 session from a parallel work stream; renewed growth is the signal to do that refactor rather than bump this number. Bumped from 1199 to 1204 for the CB-86 secret boundary: readTrace now masks the decision through redactDecision before returning it to an external reasoner, which cost five lines and closes a real leak. Note this entry did its job — the exception was set at the exact line count with no headroom, so the growth surfaced immediately rather than sliding through. Bumped from 1204 to 1215 for CB-93 run observability: the registry now publishes started/step/finished events so a surface can render a run it did not start. The fan-out itself was extracted to runRegistryObservers.ts rather than written inline, so what remains in the registry is only the eleven lines that must sit at the lifecycle points — one destructure, one import, two notifyStarted calls, three notifyFinished calls at the terminal paths, one notify in the step funnel and the subscribe entry. This is the third consecutive bump; the this-coupled refactor CB-90 owes is now overdue rather than merely tracked.
